question: How do steric effects of substrates and reagents influence enantioselectivity in the asymmetric electrophilic fluorination of allyl silanes and silyl enol ethers?
answer: Steric effects of substrates and reagents significantly influence enantioselectivity in the asymmetric electrophilic fluorination of allyl silanes and silyl enol ethers. Bulky substituents on substrates enhance enantioselectivity by restricting competing pathways and improving facial discrimination during fluorination. For example, in fluorodesilylation reactions, allyl silanes with bulky R groups (e.g., tert-butyl) achieve up to 95% ee, while less hindered groups (e.g., Me or H) yield lower enantioselectivity (72% and 51% ee, respectively). Similarly, modifying fluorinating reagents with sterically demanding groups (e.g., NFBSI vs. NFSI) improves enantioselectivity by up to 18% due to hindered reactivity and better chiral induction. Catalyst design, such as bis-cinchona alkaloids, further leverages steric interactions to stabilize transition states, favoring one enantiomer over the other. Thus, steric bulk in both substrates and reagents is critical for high enantioselectivity in these transformations.
